title: GET /Account/Logout signs the user out without a prompt, enabling logout CSRF
owner_hint: top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
rationale: ShowLogoutPrompt=false makes the anonymous GET handler call the POST logout action in-process, bypassing antiforgery. The diff restores the prompt default and only auto-signs-out when the user is authenticated, a logoutId was supplied, and the prompt was suppressed.
variants_checked: Other GET handlers are read-only or begin external auth; all state-changing POSTs keep antiforgery.
bypass_considered: A bare cross-site GET now renders the prompt and the follow-up POST needs an antiforgery token. Residual: a valid RP-initiated logoutId with ShowSignoutPrompt=false still auto-signs-out by design.
test_note: Added LogoutPromptStaysEnabled asserting the restored default.
review_reason: Restoring the prompt default fixes the root cause that made the GET handler sign out unconditionally; the added guard only strengthens the condition. The logoutId check is effectively dead given the prompt-suppression path already requires a context, and the test only asserts the static default.
